text: For Husserl, retention is a species of memory: it is a separate representational act that re-presents the just-past note before the mind.
explanation: This is false. Husserl insists that 'retention is not memory': retention involves no separate act and no re-presentation, but is a direct, non-representational holding of the just-past within the living present — a form of intuition. What the statement describes is recollection (secondary memory), the distinct representational act that brings a past event back before the mind. Collapsing the two erases exactly the distinction Husserl draws.
